content.title: About
content.content: Sugar‑free chocolate candy is a confection made from cocoa mass, sugar substitutes and flavorings. It retains the characteristic chocolate taste while containing no regular sugar, making it suitable for people monitoring blood glucose levels.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The sweets are often sweetened with stevia, erythritol or monk fruit, which have a low glycemic index.
Sugar‑free chocolate may contain a higher proportion of cocoa than regular versions, intensifying its bitter notes.
Some manufacturers add probiotics or vitamins, turning the candy into a functional snack.
In the United States, sugar‑free candies are classified as a dietary supplement only when specific claims are made.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Cocoa is high in flavonoids, which help combat free radicals and support cardiovascular health.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Sugar substitutes do not cause rapid spikes in blood glucose, beneficial for diabetics or low‑carb diets.

items.title: Contains magnesium
items.content: Cocoa provides a good source of magnesium, important for muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Mood‑enhancing
items.content: Chocolate stimulates the production of serotonin and endorphins, improving mood.

items.title: Cocoa allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to cocoa components.

items.title: Sugar substitute side effects
items.content: Erythritol and other polyols can cause gastrointestinal discomfort if consumed in excess.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Despite lacking sugar, the candy still contains fats and calories, so moderation is advised.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Sugar‑free chocolate candies can be enjoyed as a standalone snack, added to dessert platters, or used in baking as a substitute for regular chocolate. Keep them in a cool place to prevent melting.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the candies in an airtight container in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. For extended shelf life, keep them refrigerated to preserve texture and flavor.
